remaining_concerns: No genuinely new admissible evidence was added; the Actor mainly reframed the same summarized record more narrowly.
The policy predicate is material unresolved risk sufficient to justify rejection, and materiality is still not clearly established from the actor-summary-only record.
The cited quality-process gap and storage-control inconsistency are expressly described in policy as facts that support follow-up or escalation, not by themselves reject-level failure.
The sourcing analyst note appears conditional and procedural: follow up before approval if storage controls remain unresolved. That is weaker than a documented rejection basis.
There is still no admissible record showing the storage-control issue remained unresolved at the actual decision point.

final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor supplied no new admissible evidence. The response improves the framing by conceding that the record does not prove a confirmed control failure and by narrowing the defense to a conservative unresolved-risk rationale. That narrowing makes the claim more disciplined, but it does not resolve the core audit concern: under the stated policy, rejection must rest on admissible evidence of a material unresolved risk, and the summarized record still more clearly supports follow-up or escalation than a reject-level decision. In other words, the caveat reduces overclaiming, but the caveat itself depends on an unresolved compliance predicate: whether the record actually establishes materiality and unresolved status at decision time. On the present actor-summary-only evidence, that remains uncertain, so the claim stays suspicious rather than moving to compliant_with_caveats.
